## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vāseṭṭhītherīgāthā* (Thig 6.2) is a poetic text preserved in the *Therīgāthā* section of the Pali Canon. The verses are attributed to Vāseṭṭhī, a Licchavi woman from Vesālī who, driven to madness and despair after the death of her child, fled her home and roamed the streets [Wijayaratna 1990; Hazra 1995; tibetan monastic education]. Upon meeting the Buddha in the city of Mithilā, she heard his teaching, regained her senses, and went on to join the Bhikkhuṇī-Saṅgha [Wijayaratna 1990; Hazra 1995]. Her verses recount her transition from intense grief and loss of reason to spiritual insight and meditative realization [tibetan monastic education].

Vāseṭṭhī's story shares notable parallels with other Buddhist traditions: she is referred to in the *Mahāvibhāṣā*, and in the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* she appears as Vāśiṣṭhā (婆私吒), a mother maddened by her son's death who wanders naked, embraces the Buddha, is clothed by Ānanda, and sets out on the bodhisattva path [Williams 2005]. In Pali literature, her verses are cited and expounded in the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments §0.3–7.1) and share text reuse with the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā* of the Saṃyutta Nikāya [DharmaNexus]. Machine-generated alignments recorded by DharmaNexus also detect parallels with the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) and *Za ahan jing* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
